claims.text: Screen readers read the semantics tree Flutter builds alongside the widget tree; Text widgets add their words to it, and depending on the enclosing widgets two Texts become separate nodes or are merged into one node.
claims.source_hint: Flutter docs: accessibility, Semantics; flutter_test finders.dart (bySemanticsLabel: framework may combine labels)

claims.text: Semantics with a label and excludeSemantics: true replaces the descendants' semantics with that one label; with excludeSemantics false, the child Texts' words are appended to the same node after the label (name and price read twice).

Material Design (Google's design guidelines, followed by Flutter's Material widgets) recommends tap targets of at least 48x48 logical pixels; a logical pixel is a device-independent unit of roughly constant physical size.
claims.source_hint: Flutter docs: accessibility (tap target size); material/constants.dart kMinInteractiveDimension; flutter-for/android-devs (logical pixels)

claims.text: ProductTile@stage-1: Semantics(label: name, price đồng; button: onTap != null; excludeSemantics: true) > InkWell(onTap) > ConstrainedBox(minHeight: 48) > Padding(12) > Row(Expanded(Text(name)), Text(price đ)); ProductCatalog passes no onTap; list tile spans list width, grid columns >= 300 wide.

A widget test builds and lays out widgets in a simplified test environment without a device (a separate kind from a unit test). This one pumps catalogWithWidth(360), checks the first tile is >= 48 tall and bySemanticsLabel finds "Bàn phím cơ, 1250000 đồng" (String: equality); it passes.
claims.source_hint: Flutter docs: testing/overview.md (widget vs unit test); examples/don-hang @ stage-1: DonHang.App/test/product_catalog_test.dart:16-22,38-44; flutter_test finders.dart (bySemanticsLabel)

claims.text: ProductCatalog's grid gives every cell a fixed height of 72 (mainAxisExtent: 72). BoxConstraints(minHeight: 48) sets only a lower bound: in the one-column list a tile with wrapped text grows taller; in the grid it stays 72.
Accessibility built into a small reused widget like a tile carries to every screen reusing it; small targets are hard to hit for many people, so a bigger target helps all of them.
claims.source_hint: outline items 1, 3; Flutter docs ui-design-and-styling (small controls)

claims.text: InkWell makes its child respond to taps and calls onTap; Semantics.button marks the subtree as a button, and screen readers (TalkBack/VoiceOver) add the hint "button".
claims.source_hint: Flutter API docs: InkWell; semantics.dart SemanticsProperties.button
